title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants - DPP 06 (Pollination Adaptations)

questions.question: An angiospermic plant has following characteristics. Identify the type of pollination in it. P. The pollen grains are light and non-sticky Q. Presence of feathery stigma R. Nectaries absent S. Flowers have well exposed stamens
A dioecious flowering plant prevents both:
questions.explanation: Option (B) is correct: Autogamy and geitonogamy.

questions.question: Protandry is a condition in which:
options: anthers and stigma mature at the same time
anthers mature earlier than the stigma
pollens of the same flower pollinates stigma
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: anthers mature earlier than the stigma.

questions.question: Incompatibility in plants refers to:
options: The inability of a flower to develop into a fruit
The inability of two flowers to cross-pollinate
The inability of two different plant species to reproduce
The inability of pollen to germinate on the stigma of the same flower
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct: The inability of pollen to germinate on the stigma of the same flower.

questions.question: Self incompatibility:
options: Allows pollen grains of other flowers of the same plant to fertilise the ovule
Does not allow the germination of pollen grains of other species on the stigma
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: Is a genetically controlled mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following labelled parts of gynoecium determines the compatible nature of pollen?
Pistil accepts the pollen and promote post pollination event, when pollen is-
options: from same species and are self incompatible
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct: from same species.

questions.question: What does the filiform apparatus do at the entrance into the ovule?
options: It brings about opening of the pollen tube
It guides pollen tube from a synergid to egg
It helps in the entry of pollen tube into a synergid
It prevents entry of more than one pollen tube into the embryo sac
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: It helps in the entry of pollen tube into a synergid.

questions.question: The events in pollen-pistil interaction are given below (i) Pollen grain germinates to form pollen tube. (ii) Pollen tube enters the ovule through micropyle. (iii) Pollen grain reaches the stigma. (iv) Pollen tube grows through the tissues of stigma and style and reaches the ovary. The sequential order of their occurence is
Identify to in the given diagram.
options: A-Pollen tube, B-Ovary, C-Ovule, D- Antipodal cell, E-Pollen grain, F-Polar nuclei
A-Polar nuclei, B-Antipodal cell, C-Ovule, D- Ovary, E-Pollen tube, F-Pollen grain
A-Pollen grain, B-Pollen tube, C-Ovary, D- Ovule, E-Antipodal cell, F-Polar nuclei
A-Antipodal cell, B-Ovule, C-Ovary, D-Polar nuclei, E-Pollen grain, F-Pollen tube
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: A-Pollen grain, B-Pollen tube, C-Ovary, D- Ovule, E-Antipodal cell, F-Polar nuclei.

questions.question: Emasculation not required during artificial hybridisation when flower is;
Artificial hybridisation is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme. For the bisexual flower it includes the following steps in correct sequence.
options: Bagging, emasculation, pollination, rebagging → → → → → → → → → → → → A F
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: Emasculation, bagging, pollination, rebagging.
